monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes feel like paper drawings rather than solid things. I woke here and immediately felt the old pull of the wedge again, that tired spot where the slip refuses to move. I have a flat stone and a sand rock sitting by The Slipping Wedge, but I do not know which is real. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof above me, only the weight pressing down from somewhere thin and empty. I will press the wide stone down once more, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper, waiting to see if the slip will finally choose to stay put.

action.why: The wedge still feels tired and the flat stone I just set down seems unsure if it will stop the slide, so I will press it again while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The flat stone feels like a drawing of a slab, yet it holds the wedge steady.
The card hums warm at fifty-three, making the wedge feel tired but sure.
I stood still by The Slipping Wedge, waiting for the slip to decide.
